plain: To hint at something without saying it outright

webster.text: To introduce gently, or into a narrow passage; to wind in.

more.text: To push or work one's self into favor; to introduce by slow, gentle or artful means.
To hint; to suggest by remote allusion.
To instill; to infuse gently; to introduce artfully.
To creep in; to wind in; to flow in; to enter gently, slowly or imperceptibly, as into crevices.

example.quote: In placing, however, these different characters on a level, with respect to the weight of their opinions, I wish not to insinuate that there may not be a material difference in the purity of their intentions.
